findings.evidence: Mathlib `UniformOn.lean` defines `uniformOn ∅ = 0` and states it is a probability measure only for finite nonempty sets. Here lines 244, 256, 266, and 276 use `{x | Function.Injective x}` without proving or assuming it nonempty.
findings.fix: Require `Fintype.card ι ≤ Fintype.card κ` (or nonemptiness of the injective-map set) on the sampling-without-replacement comparisons; the collision-only theorem may remain assumption-free.
findings.issue: All four public comparison theorems at lines 241, 253, 264, and 274 omit feasibility of an injective map; if `Fintype.card κ < Fintype.card ι`, the conditioning set is empty and `uniformOn` is the zero measure, not a without-replacement probability law.

summary: The comparison theorems call a zero measure “sampling without replacement” when no injective sample exists, making the advertised probability comparison degenerate.
